attributes.residual: ONE NAMED MECHANISM, register-tie-break with a schedule shadow, 5 instructions at 0x424-0x440. Target: `lwz r3,gSysFlags` / `li r0,4` / `mtctr r0` / `lwz r5,gPadCur` / `rlwinm r0,r3,0,20,18` / `lis r3,gPadStartHoldTimer@ha` / `stw r0,gSysFlags` / `li r6,0` / `addi r4,r3,@lo`. Ours: `lwz r4,gSysFlags` / `li r0,4` / `lis r3,@ha` / `mtctr r0` / `rlwinm r0,r4` / `stw r0,gSysFlags` / `addi r4,r3,@lo` / `lwz r5,gPadCur` / `li r3,0`. Both sides materialize the address identically (@ha into r3, @lo into r4); the ONLY differences are (a) the gSysFlags temp is coloured r3 in the target and r4 in ours, and (b) the loop's byte-offset accumulator is r6 in the target and r3 in ours, with the `lis` consequently hoisted one slot earlier in ours and the `lwz gPadCur` sunk three slots later. Because the target keeps gSysFlags live in r3 until the rlwinm consumes it, the target is FORCED to emit `lis r3` after the mask; ours frees r3 early and the scheduler fills the slot. No source form found that pins the flag temp to r3.
